note.question: How do production and holding costs affect the optimal mechanism?
note.overview: A core problem in the area of revenue management is pricing goods in the presence of strategic customers. This paper studies this problem when customers are heterogeneous with respect to their initial valuations for the good and their time sensitivities—that is, the customers differ in both their initial valuations and the rates at which their initial valuation decreases with a delay in the purchase. In many settings, especially in fashion and electronic retail, a customer’s valuation for the product is time-sensitive and decreases over time.

models.summary: A core problem in the area of revenue management is pricing goods in the presence of strategic customers. This paper studies this problem when customers are heterogeneous with respect to their initial valuations for the good and their time sensitivities—that is, the customers differ in both their initial valuations and the rates at which their initial valuation decreases with a delay in the purchase. We also investigate the impact of production and holding costs on the optimal mechanism.

This modeling choice allows us to study the impact of strategic customers and decay in customer valuation, but it deliberately removes the element of uncertainty from the model.
